name: Earth Mother
summary: Across Azeroth, the Earth Mother’s presence lives in the land and its elements. Tauren say she shaped the world, raised the sun and moon, and guides their lives and hopes for what follows death.

sections.title: The Dawn of Creation
sections.body: Tauren creation myths say the Earth Mother shaped Azeroth before day and night, making it a haven for her coming children. She scraped her nails across the new mountains, and the first fires sparked. Her hands carved rivers and ocean beds, while her laughter gave breath to the wind. Then she lifted the primordial fogs into the sky. The first rains coaxed grass, forests, and grain from the soil.

sections.title: Sun, Moon, and the Shu'halo
sections.body:
With help from the friendly elements, the Earth Mother brought forth twins: An'she, the sun, and Mu'sha, the moon. She placed the radiant twins in her eyes, so she could rest while keeping them safe. As she opened and closed each lid, day, night, and the seasons began.

Later, she pressed her heart against the fertile earth and breathed the song of life into the land. There she created the shu'halo, the first tauren. She charged the twins and the elements to teach these young mortals to hunt, build, dance, and live in harmony with the wilds.

sections.title: Eyes in the Heavens
sections.body: In time, the Earth Mother set An'she and Mu'sha in the sky to watch over the land by day and night. Tauren say her spirit now dwells in the world's rivers, trees, plains, and mountains. Every lesser nature spirit springs from her and returns to her in the end.

sections.title: Living Legacy
sections.body: Tauren believe the Earth Mother's spirit still cradles Azeroth. Her ear listens to the winds for her children's prayers, and her heart beats within the deep stone. Tauren hunters, shamans, and druids give thanks to her for every kill and harvest. They believe all life begins in her embrace, and every tauren spirit returns to her soil upon death.

faq.answer: Tauren worship the Earth Mother as the creator at the heart of their faith. Their myths say she shaped Azeroth's landscape, brought forth the sun and moon, and created the tauren from the soil.

faq.q: What are her eyes in the sky?
faq.answer: An'she, the sun, is the Earth Mother's right eye and brings light and warmth to the world. Mu'sha, the White Lady moon, is her left eye and brings peace and slumber. Tauren myth says she set them in the heavens to watch over the land.

faq.q: Is the Earth Mother an actual living entity?
faq.answer: Tauren believe the Earth Mother is an active, loving spiritual presence throughout the natural world, stone, and winds. Shamans and druids channel nature and elemental spirits through her blessings. Whether she was a primordial giant, a world-soul, or an allegory remains a matter of faith.

faq.q: Do other races worship the Earth Mother?
aliases: do trolls believe in earth mother
faq.answer: The tauren are the Earth Mother's primary worshippers, and other peoples who commune with the land acknowledge her. Some orc shamans and centaur invoke her name respectfully, and her blessings are often exchanged throughout the Horde.

faq.q: What do tauren believe happens after death?
faq.answer: Tauren believe every soul returns to the Earth Mother after death, since all living things were born from her touch. Traditional rites commit the deceased to the land, trusting their spirits to rest in her eternal embrace.

angles.text: As a shu'halo, your society's ways, from respect for prey to the council of chieftains, are rooted in the Earth Mother's law, sacrifice, and enduring love.
As a tauren druid, your bond with nature is direct communion with the Earth Mother's living body, answering her ancient call to preserve the land's balance.
As a tauren shaman, you honor the Earth Mother alongside the elemental spirits, remembering that wind, water, fire, and stone were her first companions.
As an orc or jungle troll in the Horde, you know tauren reverence for the Earth Mother through your alliance with Mulgore. You may invoke her name as a respectful blessing.
